An Exceptional Childhood for Girls & Boys Aged 3 to 11
Headmaster's welcome
At Willington Prep, we have only one purpose: we are wholly dedicated to giving every pupil an exceptional childhood, rich with opportunities and experiences. This fundamental purpose resonates through every aspect of our school life and shapes our commitment to our pupils and their families.
Nestled in the vibrant community of Wimbledon, Willington Prep is a co-educational haven for children aged 3 to 11, celebrating 140 years, in 2025, of nurturing young minds and hearts. Our embrace of co-education in 2020 marked a new chapter in our story, one that reinforces our belief in a family-oriented environment where every child matters.
At the heart of a Willington childhood is the happiness and self-assurance of our pupils. Guided by the enduring values of kindness, honesty, respect, and humility, we strive not only to educate but to inspire a lifelong journey of learning and discovery.
Our exceptional team of educators brings to life a broad and vibrant curriculum, supported by a rich tapestry of co-curricular activities. We see childhood as the very essence of life's foundation, a time to be valued, filled with wonder and growth. It is this philosophy that underpins our ethos: to cherish and elevate every moment of this pivotal stage of life.
While other schools may offer co-education, our approach is seasoned with our unique celebration of childhood, honouring the individuality of each young learner. This commitment has not only set us apart but also deepened our resolve to nurture a generation of confident, compassionate, and culturally aware individuals. Our children are multinational, multi-faith and multi-talented.
Thank you for your interest in Willington Prep, where childhood is not just a phase, but the heart of our 'why'.
Mr Keith Brown Headmaster E: headmaster@willingtonschool.co.uk

Preparing for the next step. This Wednesday, we look forward to welcoming representatives from 17 senior schools to Willington for our Future Schools Showcase, an evening dedicated to helping our parents explore the opportunities ahead. Choosing the right senior school is an important journey, and one we support carefully throughout the Prep years. From specialist teaching and academic preparation to individual guidance and conversations with families, our approach is designed to help every child move on with confidence. Our Showcase is an important part of that process, giving parents the opportunity to meet senior school representatives, ask questions and discover the breadth of choices available. At Willington, we believe in preparing children for their future while ensuring they enjoy the childhood they have today. Learning in Balance. We are delighted to welcome the following senior schools: @epsomcollegeuk @emanuel.school @wimbledonhighschoolgdst @kingswimbledon @hamptonschooluk @kgs1561 @reedsschool_cobham @marymountlondon @stjohnsleatherhead @surbitonhighschool @claremontfancourt @whitgiftschool @notredamecobham @thomasscollege @putneyhighschool @trinitycroydon @hallifordschoolshepperton #WillingtonPrep #FutureSchools #11Plus #LearningInBalance
Build, programme, test, rethink. 🤖 With specialist teaching in Years 5 and 6, LEGO robotics brings STEM to life, combining logical thinking with creativity and practical problem-solving. Our Year 6 children work together to turn ideas into movement, testing and refining their designs along the way. Learning in Balance: curious minds, purposeful challenge and the enjoyment of discovery. #WillingtonPrep #LearningInBalance #STEM #LEGORobotics
Harvest is a time to give thanks – and to think about how we can help others in our community. This Friday, we will come together for our Harvest Festival and continue a longstanding Willington tradition of supporting @wimbledonguild . Children and staff are invited to bring in practical donations which will help local people in need, from older members of the community to families and individuals receiving welfare support. For our children, it is also an important opportunity to see our school values in action: understanding that even a simple contribution can make a difference to someone else. A reminder to parents: please send your child in on Friday with the item allocated to their year group, in a bag they can carry themselves. The children will add their donations to our Harvest table in the Hall ready for Assembly. Thank you, as always, for your support and generosity. #WillingtonPrep #HarvestFestival #Kindness #Community

Aims, Ethos & School Policies
We are committed to creating an exceptional childhood experience in a supportive atmosphere, guided by our school values of honesty, respect, kindness, and humility. Empowering each child to unlock their innate talents and abilities across all facets of life, our comprehensive approach embraces academic, creative, and sporting accomplishments while fostering self-confidence and happiness in every child. We aim to prepare them for a bright future, offering an excellent foundation for lifelong learning and success, and instilling these essential values that will serve them well throughout their lives.

Drama
Drama at Willington allows the children to express themselves in a creative and collaborative way, through movement and interaction with others. The subject promotes imagination and multi-sensory learning and develops essential life-long skills such as creativity, enquiry, communication, empathy, self confidence, cooperation, leadership and negotiation. Above all, we aim to make Drama fun and an enjoyable, memorable learning experience for our pupils.
In the Pre-Prep department, Drama is integrated into the curriculum, with opportunities for exploring stories, role-play, and developing speaking and listening during circle time activities. All Pre-Prep children perform in Nativity style productions at the end of the Autumn term. In Years 3 and 4, Drama is used as a cross-curricular tool, as well as a vehicle for developing the pupils’ public speaking skills and poetry performance.
In Year 5 and 6, the pupils have a standalone Drama lesson per week. These lessons provide the children with opportunities to express their thoughts, opinions and emotions in a supportive environment, as well as providing meaningful cross-curricular links to other subjects such as English, History and PSHE. Previous cross-curricular topics have included Remembrance Day, the Anglo-Saxons, The Rainforest and Bullying. We also aim to develop the pupils’ speaking and listening skills by exploring key dramatic techniques such as voice and projection, gesture, mime and script work.
The Year 4 Production offers pupils an exciting introduction to a more formal style of performance. It provides valuable experience in stagecraft, teamwork, and presentation, helping to build confidence and prepare them for the larger-scale Year 6 Leavers’ Production. Previous Year 4 performances have included shows such as Wind in the Willows and Pantastic. The Year 6 Leavers’ Production is a highlight of the school year and a joyful celebration of our oldest pupils’ time at Willington. It offers them a final opportunity to showcase their talents, both on and off the stage, and to take pride in all they have achieved during their Willington journey. Previous productions have included The Tempest, The Greatest Show and I’m An 11-Year Old, Get Me Out of Here!
We offer various extra-curricular clubs such as LAMDA for Years 1-6, Podcasting for KS2, using our new school radio recording equipment, and for our younger pupils, Drama and Movement. In addition, we offer one-to-one peripatetic LAMDA sessions. We also run a Drama scholarship programme, for those pupils wishing to apply for 11+ Drama scholarships.
Co-Curriculum›

Music
In the Music Department we provide a wide range of musical opportunities, both curricular and extra-curricular, for every pupil in the school. The overriding ethos is to be inclusive and make music accessible to all, whilst offering challenges to our gifted musicians. Studying a wide range of musical styles offers plenty of opportunity for the three tenets of Music Education: composing, performing and listening to/appraising music. Focus on developing instrumental and vocal skills, music literacy and vocabulary, and confidence is essential. Trips, concerts and school performances are an important part of the curriculum providing occasions for pupils to experience and appreciate live music. Working with the Drama department, musical productions are also annual features in the school calendar.

Governors
Ms Faith Pengelly, Co-Chair of Governors Finance & General Purpose Committee
Faith joined the Board in 2023 and sits on the Finance and General Purpose Committee. Faith has an MBA from Henley Management College. She has a background in financial services/corporate finance and has over 25 years’ experience working as a qualified Company Secretary. Faith has lived in the Wimbledon area for over 35 years.
Contact: chairofgovernors@willingtonschool.co.uk
Christopher Bates, Co-Chair of Governors Academic Committee
Giles Grindlay, Independent Governor Finance & General Purpose Committee
Kate Hopper-Reeve, Independent Governor Allergy Governor
Suzanne Le Jeune, Independent Governor Finance & General Purpose Committee
Ed Mills, Independent Governor
Katy Morgan, Independent Governor Pastoral & Safeguarding Committee Safeguarding Governor
Katy Morgan is the Head of Lower School at St John's School, Northwood. She qualified as a teacher in 1993, specialising in primary education. She is currently leading a large department caring for pupils from Nursery to Year 4. She joined the Board of Governors in June 2022.
Charmaine Pollock, Independent Governor
Charmaine joined the Board of Governors in March 2026. She is an employment lawyer and a Partner at Farrer & Co LLP. Charmaine has called the Wimbledon and Raynes Park areas home since 2008 when she moved to the UK from Australia.
Rhys Tomlin, Independent Governor Compliance and Health & Safety Committee
Rhys has been the site manager at King's College, Wimbledon for over seventeen years. He joined the Board in June 2022 and sits on the Compliance and Health & Safety Committee
Ian White, Independent Governor Pastoral & Safeguarding Committee
Ian White joined the Board of Governors in July 2022. Having previously taught at Tiffin School and St George’s College, Weybridge, Ian is currently Deputy Head (Co-Curricular and Logistics) at St John’s School, Leatherhead where he has also previously held the roles of Assistant Head (Upper School), Head of Department, Head of Lower School and Housemaster of a Senior Boys’ House.
Ian was educated locally at Wallington County Grammar School and graduated with a Sports and Exercise Science degree from the University of Portsmouth and a Masters in Educational Leadership and Management from the University of Bath. Additionally he holds a Level 3 Designated Safeguarding Lead (NSPCC) and Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) qualification.
Ian is married to Helen, also a teacher, and they have two young boys, as well as an energetic Cocker Spaniel called Reggie, which keeps them busy when not in the classroom.
Ian brings a wide knowledge of educational and pastoral matters to the Board and sits on the Pastoral and Safeguarding Committee.
The governors may be contacted via the Bursar & Clerk to the Governors: bursar@willingtonschool.co.uk
The Governors may be contacted via the Clerk to the Governors, Colleen Woodley via email to bursar@willingtonschool.co.uk.

Art & Design Technology
The Art and Design Technology department inspires children through a broad and inspiring curriculum. We aim to provide experiences which support individuality and a journey of artistic growth. Through exploring a broad range of techniques, styles and approaches, the children will experiment, invent and create, allowing them the opportunity to express themselves. The children will study historical, cultural and current Art projects, learning to think laterally and inspiring their imagination.
We will explore techniques and styles including drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, digital and mixed media in Art, whilst discovering a wide range of tools and materials in Design Technology, such as LEGO, woodwork, textiles and graphic design. Through studying different artists and designers, children are encouraged to use new vocabulary to discuss their thoughts and opinions. All of this is achieved in our specialist Art classroom.
Each year, we celebrate our love and appreciation of the arts through an annual Arts Festival, which offers the opportunity for a diverse range of artist-led workshops across three days, with trips to different London galleries and exhibitions. This is a wonderful experience for every child to be immersed in creativity. At the end of the school year, we celebrate the children’s achievements with a whole school Art exhibition - where every child will have a piece of Art on show.
An Art Scholarship programme is in place for those who demonstrate a passion and keen interest in Art. There is also an enrichment programme which includes painting, textiles, warhammer and creative clubs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Willington Independent Prep School- Senior Leadership Team
pageCache.text:
Senior Leadership Team
Keith Brown Headmaster Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL)
Keith Brown joined Willington in September 2018 having served as Deputy Headmaster at St John's Northwood (a Merchant Taylor's School). Keith brings a wealth of experience to the School having taught every age from Nursery to Upper Sixth over the past 27 years.
Since joining Willington, Keith has driven the School forward with the move to 11+, co-education, the launch of the Nursery and the provision of in-house catering. With a keen personal interest in technology in education, Keith oversaw the school’s swift and successful transition to remote learning during lockdown and has introduced a number of new school platforms to benefit the entire Willington community. Keith enjoys meeting with current parents to discuss future schools for their children and has built strong relationships with all the senior schools. Holding individual meetings with prospective parents ensures Keith stays informed with the needs and expectations of the new generations coming through the school.
Hailing from the Scottish Borders town of Melrose, Keith is married to Anne and they have four grown up children. In his spare time Keith enjoys cycling and is a keen musician, regularly playing in a band to raise money for charity. Passionate about all sports, Keith is an avid rugby fan.
Eleanor Henery Deputy Head Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)
Eleanor Henery joined Willington School in 2020 having spent many happy years at Kingswood House School, Epsom, overseeing Nursery to Year 4. Ellie has used her previous Senior Leadership Team experience (which included assisting architects with school buildings and introducing a broader curriculum range) to launch the new Willington Nursery and to integrate the learning into a two-year programme with Reception. As a hands-on manager, she has overseen the transition of the first co-ed cohorts into Nursery and Reception in 2021 and, by maintaining regular teaching slots in the pre-prep she understands the individual needs of the pupils, as well as the expectations of the parents. Ellie has launched the new School Council programme and works hard on the School’s charity initiatives.
Eleanor is born and bred in Epsom and is a keen athlete who enjoys spending time running in the country side along with outdoor swimming. She has completed 3 marathons and raised a great deal of money for charity.
Colleen Woodley Bursar
Colleen Woodley joined Willington in June 2023 having been a Bursar for 10 years at Thomas More College, an Independent co-educational day school based in South Africa catering for 1200 pupils ranging from 4 months to 18 years old.
In her career Colleen has been an audit partner at an Auditing firm, and has worked as Financial Manager for an International CCTV company and various manufacturing companies.
Colleen is a qualified Chartered accountant registered with both SAICA in South Africa and ICAEW in the UK. She was born and raised in Durban, South Africa, but her family is originally from Norwich. She enjoys playing golf, sewing and travelling.
Lucy Walton Registrar & Director of Communications EA to the Headmaster
Part of the Willington community since 2007 (both her sons attended the school and are now thriving at Cranleigh and Lancaster University), Lucy Walton joined the staff as Admissions Officer in 2016. Lucy plays a full role in the life of the school and was part of the team that oversaw the school’s recent co-educational transition and nursery launch. Joining the Senior Leadership Team in early 2021, her role encompasses all aspects of new pupil recruitment as well as the marketing of the school and external relations.
Lucy was born and raised in Kent and moved to London in 1995 to work in a number of corporate positions. Her last role before leaving the workplace to raise her family was working for Marriott International in launching and marketing a five star hotel in central London. A natural 'early adopter', Lucy thrives on new experiences. She is an avid reader and enjoys travel adventures with her family.
Senior Leadership Team›

The Nursery
Our Nursery provides a warm and stimulating introduction to school life, helping children to settle confidently into a larger school environment from an early age. Being part of the wider Willington community allows children to become familiar with school routines, spaces and staff, supporting a smooth and happy transition into Reception.
Nursery children learn and play alongside a diverse group of peers, developing important social and communication skills at this formative stage. Through a carefully planned Early Years curriculum, they begin to build strong foundations for learning, while also developing independence, confidence and a sense of belonging.
Children benefit from specialist teaching in French, Music and PE, making full use of our hall and playgrounds. They take part in outdoor education twice a term with the rest of the Pre-Prep and enjoy a range of trips throughout the year, enriching their learning and encouraging curiosity and a love of learning.

The Prep
Pupils delve deeper into a wide range of subjects, taught by their class teacher in Years 3 and 4, with a continuation of specialist teaching in specific subjects. Preparing Year 5 and Year 6 pupils for the next transition, a senior school model is followed, with each subject taught by a specialist teacher.

Reception
Our Reception curriculum is carefully designed to support curiosity, confidence and a love of learning, building on the strong foundations laid in Nursery. Learning is rooted in the Early Years Foundation Stage and supports children’s academic, social and emotional development as they grow in independence.
The curriculum focuses on the three prime areas of learning — communication and language, physical development, and personal, social and emotional development — which are strengthened through literacy, mathematics, understanding the world, and expressive arts and design.
Children enjoy daily phonics lessons using the Monster Phonics scheme, building on their early phonics knowledge in a lively and engaging way. Teaching is delivered through a balance of whole-class learning, small group work and independent exploration, supported by qualified teaching assistants who know each child well. Teachers closely observe and track progress, introducing handwriting and letter formation through creative, hands-on approaches.
Children also benefit from specialist teaching in Music and Movement, Art, ICT, French and PE, taught in subject-specific spaces. Weekly visits to local school fields and regular trips further enrich learning, helping children connect classroom experiences with the wider world. Two free enrichment sessions each week offer opportunities for extended activities and deeper engagement.
